title: Polymorphic inference
gist: A positioning piece: inference should change form as models, traffic and chips change, instead of shipping one hand-tuned configuration. It names the Together Compiler as the first piece, with adaptive speculative decoding, workload-aware model routing and per-customer post-training to follow, and calls the compiler loop recursive self-improvement at production scale.
changes: Supplies the churn argument in one statistic and the vocabulary, static against polymorphic, that others are picking up. It is also the most explicit commercial claim to the RSI label.
caveats: No performance numbers of its own. The RSI claim is the company's characterisation; the companion technical post does not use the phrase or describe agents improving themselves. Most of the agenda is planned, not shipped, and per-customer compilation is a limited beta.

numbers.metric: Share of OpenRouter traffic on models released in the last three months
numbers.baseline: market observation cited by Together, not independently checked

bears_on.note: If four-fifths of traffic is on models under three months old, nothing hand-tuned stays relevant for long.
Claims the label outright; the evidence for the recursive part is not shown.
Per-customer continuous compilation exists, but only as a limited beta on request.
